title: 210. Matchsticks to Square

examples.explanation: You can form a square with side length 2: three sides use a single stick of length 2 each, and the fourth side uses two sticks of length 1.
You cannot find a way to form a square with all the matchsticks.

hints: The total length must be divisible by 4 for a square to exist.
Treat each matchstick as belonging to one of 4 buckets (the sides). The choice of which bucket a stick joins can be shared with bitmask DP to avoid re-searching repeated partial states.
Sort the sticks descending so that large sticks are placed first and prune the search early.
